title: The launcher's elementwise shape defaults override the contraction contract's own extents, handing every task in that family a starter the Metal verifier must refuse

evidence.note: preflight of the documented contraction command line (--depth 256, no shape flags) on a clean v98 checkout: baseline preparation refused, METAL_PRIVATE_STORAGE_LIMIT blocking at the starter's full second-operand load; the launcher's generic defaults (rows 128, columns 1024) had overridden the contract's (rows 1024, depth 128, columns 64)

same named refusal at columns 64 with depth 256: the starter materializes the whole second operand per program, so the binding constraint is the product K*N against the 1024 lane-owned FP32 bound, not the column count alone
columns 32 with depth 256 (K*N = 8192) is the admitting boundary for this starter: all four contraction tasks preflight green at r128-k256-n32, which is how the v98 batch was launched
replay under the successor: the same bare command line resolves to contraction-gemm-fp32-metal-m1-pro-r1024-k128-n64-v1 (the contract's own triple) and the baseline preflight admits

observation: Every contraction task was unlaunchable on Metal through the documented command line, while the Triton route ran the same defaults fine -- the bug is in the launcher, not the contract. The contraction contract declares its own extents precisely so the starter's materialized second operand stays inside the Metal lane-owned storage bound; launch_task.py's argparse defaults (128 x 1024, the elementwise tile) silently overrode them. The verifier's refusal was always correct, named and inspectable; the default resolution made it fire on every bare invocation. Explicit shape flags keep that named refusal, which stays the right answer for user-chosen shapes.
proposed_change: Executor successor: absent --rows/--columns resolve per family -- contraction tasks take the contract's 1024/64, every other family keeps the elementwise 128/1024; explicit flags still win and keep the verifier's named hardware-conformance refusal.
verified_by: Replay: tools/launch_task.py --task gemm --depth 128 with no shape flags under Executor v99 resolves r1024-k128-n64 and the baseline preflight admits (probe-v99-default workload.json); tests/contracts/test_task_launch.py::test_contraction_tasks_default_to_their_own_admitting_shape pins the resolution for both families and for explicit overrides; green in the 130-test launch/claude/contraction selection. Landed in the same change as this finding on main.
verification_plan: Bug tick, replay-verified: the cited bare preflight command under the successor must build its baseline without touching the starter or the verifier; an explicit shape combination that exceeds the storage bound must keep the named METAL_PRIVATE_STORAGE_LIMIT refusal.
